name: Western Europe & the Atlantic Coast
wars: Napoleonic Wars (1803–15) · World War I, the Western Front (1914–18) · World War II, the Battle of France and D-Day (1940–45)
notes: The British Isles to Poland, Scandinavia's southern tip to Gibraltar. Dense cities, the Alps and the Pyrenees, and the Channel between rivals.

name: Eastern Europe & Russia
wars: Napoleon's invasion of Russia (1812) · World War I, the Eastern Front (1914–18) · Russian Civil War (1918–22) · World War II, from Barbarossa to Stalingrad and Kursk (1941–45)
notes: Berlin to the Volga and the Black Sea to the Gulf of Finland. A vast plain cut by great rivers, the Vistula, Dnieper, Don and Volga, with the Carpathians and the Caucasus along the southern edge and long marches between cities.

name: The Mediterranean & North Africa
wars: Punic Wars (264–146 BC) · The Crusades (1096–1291) · Battle of Lepanto (1571) · World War II: North Africa, Sicily and Italy (1940–45)
notes: The inland sea of the ancient and modern world, from Gibraltar to the Levant. Italy, the Balkans and the African coast face each other across short, contested crossings, with Malta, Sicily, Crete and Cyprus as the stepping stones, the Nile to the south and the Atlas, the Alps and the Taurus around the edges.

name: The North Atlantic
wars: The Battle of the Atlantic, World Wars I and II (1914–18, 1939–45) · The age of sail, from the Armada to Trafalgar · The Cold War and the GIUK Gap
notes: Mostly ocean: the convoy road between North America and Europe, with Newfoundland, Iceland, Ireland and the British Isles as the stepping stones. Win the sea and the land follows.

name: The Pacific
wars: World War II in the Pacific (1941–45): Pearl Harbor, Midway, Guadalcanal, the Philippines and the road to Japan · The Russo-Japanese War (1904–05)
notes: The widest theater: Japan, China and the East Indies to Australia, New Zealand and Hawaii, with a thousand islands between and oceans of sea power. Carriers, transports and island hopping decide it.

name: East Asia
wars: The Sino-Japanese Wars (1894–95, 1937–45) · The Russo-Japanese War (1904–05) · World War II in China · The Korean War (1950–53)
notes: China, Korea and Japan around the Yellow Sea: great river valleys, the long Chinese coast, the Korean peninsula pointing at Japan, and the steppe and mountains behind.

name: Korea
wars: The Korean War (1950–53) · The First Sino-Japanese War (1894–95) · The Russo-Japanese War (1904–05) · The Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–98)
notes: A small, fast theater: one mountainous peninsula between China, Japan and the sea, with the Yalu and Han rivers and Inchon and Pusan on the coast. A good first map to learn on.

name: Southeast Asia
wars: The Vietnam War (1955–75) · World War II: Malaya, Singapore and Burma (1941–45) · The First Indochina War (1946–54)
notes: Jungle, rivers and islands: the Mekong and Irrawaddy, the long Vietnamese coast and the Malay peninsula, with the Philippines and the East Indies to the east and south.

name: The Middle East & the Persian Gulf
wars: World War I: Gallipoli to Arabia and Palestine (1914–18) · The Arab–Israeli Wars (1948–73) · The Iran–Iraq War (1980–88) · The Gulf Wars (1990–91, 2003)
notes: Desert, oil and the narrow seas: the Nile to the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea and Suez, the Tigris and Euphrates, and the mountains of Anatolia and Iran around the edge.

name: Eastern North America
wars: The American Revolution (1775–83) · The War of 1812 · The American Civil War (1861–65)
notes: From the Mississippi to the Atlantic and the Gulf to the Great Lakes: the Appalachians, the Ohio and Mississippi rivers and a long coast. Here the players are the Union, the Confederacy and Canada.

name: The Caribbean & Central America
wars: The Spanish–American War (1898) · The Banana Wars and the Panama Canal (1900s) · The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) · The U-boat war in the Caribbean (1942–43)
notes: A sea of islands and short crossings between Florida, Mexico and South America: Cuba, Hispaniola and Jamaica, the Panama isthmus, and the passages that every convoy had to use.

name: India & the Indian Ocean
wars: The Seven Years' War in India (1756–63) · The Indian Rebellion (1857) · World War II: Burma and India (1942–45) · The Indo-Pakistani Wars (1947–71)
notes: The Indian subcontinent and the ocean around it: the Himalayas to the north, the Ganges and Indus plains, Ceylon, the Arabian coast and the sea lanes from Aden to Singapore.

name: Scandinavia & the Baltic
wars: The Great Northern War (1700–21) · The Finnish War (1808–09) · The Winter War and the invasion of Norway (1939–40) · The Cold War
notes: Fjords, forests and lakes around the Baltic: Norway and Sweden, Finland and Denmark, with the Baltic Sea, the Danish straits and the Gulf of Finland as the stage for sea power.

name: Africa
wars: The Scramble for Africa and the colonial wars (1880–1914) · The Boer Wars (1880–81, 1899–1902) · World War II: East Africa and the Western Desert (1940–43)
notes: A whole continent: the Sahara and the Nile, the Congo and the Great Lakes, the Ethiopian highlands, the Cape and the long coasts. Distances are huge and cities far apart.

name: South America & the South Atlantic
wars: The Wars of Independence (1808–26) · The War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70) · The War of the Pacific (1879–84) · The Falklands War (1982)
notes: The Andes down the west, the Amazon and the Pampas, and a long South Atlantic coast out to the Falklands. A continent with a great jungle in the middle and the sea on three sides.

name: The Balkans, Black Sea & Anatolia
wars: The Crimean War (1853–56) · The Balkan Wars (1912–13) · World War I: Gallipoli and the Salonika front (1915–18) · World War II: the invasion of Greece and Crete (1941)
notes: Straits, peninsulas and mountains: the Bosphorus and Dardanelles, the Aegean islands, the Danube, and the Black Sea ringed by Turkey, the Balkans, Ukraine and the Caucasus.

name: The World
wars: World War II, a global war (1939–45) · The Cold War · The Age of Sail and the empires
notes: The whole Earth on one map, wrapping east to west: every ocean, every continent and the great powers. Play it on the large grid, and expect long voyages, long wars and cities far apart.
